bhtStats.assetTitle: Asset used to measure subsequent performance
bhtStats.p1: The BHT Index measures market risk from 0 to 100: low (green) = cheap and calm, high (red) = expensive and dangerous.
bhtStats.p2: This table groups the days in the range by BHT level and shows what happened to the {asset} ({note}) over the following year and over 3 years (only days whose horizon has already elapsed): the worst (min), the typical (avg) and the best (max), plus the CAGR (average yearly return over 3 years).
bhtStats.p3spx: The reading is simple: when the BHT was low (20–35), the following year gained ~+37% on average; when it was high (65 or more), the following year barely gained or lost.
bhtStats.p3other: The reading is simple: compare the 1Y avg between low (green) and high (red) bands: if the green ones return much more, the BHT anticipates this asset well.
bhtStats.compass: Use it as a compass: <g>green = opportunity</g>, <r>red = caution</r>. Historical and hypothetical results; they do not guarantee future returns.
bhtStats.summaryBht: {from} → {to} · {n1} days with mature 1Y · {n3} with mature 3Y ({span}) · {asset} performance at 1 and 3 years by BHT band.
bhtStats.capeIntro: Same reading grouped by Shiller CAPE (price / 10-year earnings): low CAPE = cheap market, high CAPE = expensive market. Score = risk points contributed by that CAPE (0 cheap – 100 extreme).
bhtStats.summaryCape: {from} → {to} · {n1} days with CAPE and mature 1Y · {n3} with mature 3Y · {asset} performance at 1 and 3 years by CAPE.

tips.schiller_pe: CAPE = Price / 10-year average of real earnings. >30 overvalued, 20-30 normal, <20 cheap. Ratio = CAPE/mean3y.
tips.pe_ratio: S&P 500 PE = Price / trailing 12m EPS. High = market expensive vs earnings. Complements CAPE (short term).
tips.fwd_pe_ratio: Forward PE = Price / estimated 12m EPS (operating, S&P consensus). >22 expensive, 17-22 normal, <17 cheap. Looks at expectations, not the past. Below the 10y average (~19) = reasonable.
tips.inflation: CPI YoY = (CPI_t / CPI_(t−12) -1)*100. >3% pressures the Fed to raise rates. Monthly FRED CPIAUCSL data.
tips.core_inflation: Core CPI excluding food/energy. More stable; the Fed watches it to set rates.
tips.fed_rate: Fed Target Upper (DFEDTARU). 0.25% in 2008-2015 ZIRP, today ~3.75%. Rises to curb inflation.
tips.treasury_30y: 30Y Momentum: 30Y Treasury level + delta vs 6M MA. Accelerating up = brake on the economy and liquidity (risk); falling = relief. Basis for valuing stocks vs bonds.
tips.vix: VIX = S&P 500 implied volatility. >30 panic, <15 complacency.
tips.GSPC: S&P 500 (^GSPC) = index of 500 large US companies. Market benchmark.
tips.IXIC: Nasdaq (^IXIC) = tech-heavy. More volatile than the S&P.
tips.TQQQ: TQQQ = 3× QQQ daily. Decays with volatility; only for short-term tactics.
tips.QQQ: QQQ = Nasdaq-100. Base for the Mallik signal.
tips.SPY: SPY = S&P 500 ETF. Buy & hold benchmark.
tips.JEPQ: JEPQ = Nasdaq with covered calls + yield. Inception 2022-05-03.
tips.DFEDTARU: Fed Target Upper = top of the Fed rate range. 0.25% during 2008-2015 ZIRP; rises to curb inflation, falls to rescue.
tips.DGS2: 2Y Momentum: 2Y Treasury level + delta vs 6M MA. Rising fast = tightening priced in (risk); falling from high = relief (opportunity). Anticipates the Fed. 2Y > 10Y = inverted curve.
tips.DGS10: 10Y Treasury = risk-free rate. Base for HY 10Y+OAS.
tips.DGS30: 30Y Treasury = 30-year US government bond. Level + delta vs 6M MA: rising slows the economy and liquidity (risk); falling brings relief. Basis for valuing stocks vs bonds.
tips.CPIAUCSL: CPI YoY = (CPI_t / CPI_(t−12) -1)*100, headline inflation. >3% pressures the Fed to raise rates. Monthly FRED data.
tips.M2SL: M2 = broad money supply (cash + deposits + money market, $ trillions, monthly FRED). YoY >4% and accelerating + M0 expanding = tailwind: −10 bonus to the gauge (opportunity).
tips.BOGMBASE: M0 = monetary base (cash + bank reserves, monthly FRED). 3M Δ >+5% with M2 >8% = Fed bazooka −20; >+30% = mega-bazooka −25. If 3M Δ ≤ 0 it vetoes the tailwind.
tips.DCOILWTICO: WTI = oil $/barrel (daily FRED). Ratio vs 36M SMA: shock ≥1.45 → +10, expensive ≥1.20 → +5, cheap <0.90 → −5, relief <0.70 → −10 to the gauge. The +10 requires the previous month already expensive (anti-spike guard).
tips.CPILFESL: Core CPI excluding food and energy. More stable; it is what the Fed watches to set rates.
tips.BAMLH0A0HYM2: HY OAS = high-yield risk premium over Treasuries. >5% stress (2008/2020). Proxy BAA10Y*1.91 before 2023.
tips.BAMLH0A0HYM2EY: HY Effective Yield = total HY yield (coupon+price). What HY companies pay.
tips.GDP: GDP = US quarterly nominal GDP (FRED GDP, $ billions SAAR). >4% nominal strong, <2% weak. Shown with nominal and real YoY.
tips.GDPC1: GDPC1 = real GDP (inflation-adjusted, 2017 $ billions). >2% expansion, <0% recession. FRED GDPC1; real YoY = volume growth.
tips.FINRA_DEBIT: FINRA Debit = debit balances in margin accounts (FINRA, $ millions). High = elevated leverage, margin-call risk. Monthly data, FINRA Excel. 1997→today.
tips.MARGIN_GDP: Leverage/GDP = FINRA Debit / nominal GDP. ≥5% extreme (leveraged euphoria, crash risk), 4-5% very high, 3-4% elevated, 2-3% normal, <2% low. Anticipates deleveraging.
tips.MSACSR: Months of supply of new US homes (FRED MSACSR, monthly). >6m = oversupply (cold market, falling prices), 4-6m balanced, <4m shortage (hot market). Anticipates slowdowns in construction and consumption.
tips.VIXCLS: VIX = 30-day S&P 500 implied volatility (FRED VIXCLS, daily). >30 panic (opportunity), 15-20 normal, <15 complacency.
tips.FEAR_GREED: CNN Fear & Greed 0-100 (daily, ~1Y history). <25 extreme fear (opportunity), 25-45 fear, 45-55 neutral, 55-75 greed, >75 extreme greed (risk).
tips.NYSE_ADV_VOL: Volume of NYSE stocks that rose (WSJ, shares/day). Base of Net Advancing Volume.
tips.NYSE_DEC_VOL: Volume of NYSE stocks that fell (WSJ, shares/day).
tips.NSDQ_ADV_VOL: Volume of Nasdaq stocks that rose (WSJ, shares/day).
tips.NSDQ_DEC_VOL: Volume of Nasdaq stocks that fell (WSJ, shares/day).
tips.SPX_ADV_VOL: Volume of S&P 500 constituents that rose (shares/day, 1993→today). Base of Net Advancing Volume.
tips.SPX_DEC_VOL: Volume of S&P 500 constituents that fell (shares/day, 1993→today).

b0.label: Extreme Fear (High Opportunity)
b0.advice: Extreme fear tends to be the best opportunity: consider entering more strongly into QQQ, TQQQ or SOXX after confirming bottoms and oversold conditions with CAPE and RSI. Margin only makes sense if you tolerate high volatility.

b1.label: Fear (Opportunity)
b1.advice: Favorable zone: you may consider moderate margin and leveraged ETFs, avoiding extreme margin. It is worth waiting for a reversal to an uptrend before buying QQQ, TQQQ or undervalued quality companies.

b2.label: Neutral
b2.advice: No clear signal: we suggest not increasing leveraged ETFs or margin (TQQQ, SOXL). Holding positions and building cash and defensives is usually the base strategy.

b3.label: Greed (Risk)
b3.advice: Rising risk: consider trimming QQQ/TQQQ/SOXX and lowering margin, keeping at least 10% in cash or SGOV to take advantage of opportunities.

b4.label: Extreme Greed (High Risk)
b4.advice: High risk: we suggest removing margin and keeping leveraged ETFs below 20%; moving 20–40% to defensives (SGOV/IB01 or SCHD depending on your profile), building cash for drawdowns and gradually trimming expensive stocks and ETFs as the CAPE Ratio rises.
